question:
A CE amplifier is biased using a voltage-divider network for better stability. The circuit has $V_{CC}=12\,\text{V}$, $R_C=2.0\,\text{k}\Omega$, $R_E=1.0\,\text{k}\Omega$, $R_1=100\,\text{k}\Omega$ (from $V_{CC}$ to base) and $R_2=20\,\text{k}\Omega$ (from base to ground). Assume $V_{BE}=0.7\,\text{V}$ and that the divider is stiff so base current loading is neglected.

(a) Find the base voltage $V_B$ using the divider relation.

(b) Find $V_E$, $I_E$ and estimate $I_C\approx I_E$.

(c) Find $V_C$ and $V_{CE}$ and comment whether the transistor is in active region.

(d) If transistor $\beta$ increases significantly (say doubles) due to replacement, explain qualitatively (using the role of $R_E$) why the operating point does not change drastically.

(e) Draw the circuit and mark the DC current directions and key node voltages.

options.A: $V_B\approx 2.0\,\text{V}$, $V_E\approx 1.3\,\text{V}$, $I_E\approx 1.3\,\text{mA}$, $I_C\approx 1.3\,\text{mA}$; $V_C\approx 9.4\,\text{V}$ and $V_{CE}\approx 8.1\,\text{V}$ so active; $R_E$ provides negative feedback for stability.
options.B: $V_B\approx 10.0\,\text{V}$, $V_E\approx 9.3\,\text{V}$, $I_E\approx 9.3\,\text{mA}$; transistor is always saturated; $R_E$ increases instability.
options.D: $V_B\approx 2.0\,\text{V}$ but $I_E$ cannot be found without $\beta$; voltage-divider bias does not work without knowing $\beta$.
